title: The Lost Escarpment
premise: Orsen Blackwood, a bush pilot with a buried past, ferries medicine and rumors into a remote interior where the law is a rumor itself. When dying prospector Elias Marsh trades him a map to the Lost Escarpment—a plateau rumored to hold both gold and evidence of a massacre the mining company buried—for a promise to deliver it to the prospector's estranged daughter, Orsen's invisibility shatters. Hunted by company enforcers and betrayed by the stranger who joins them, Orsen and the daughter, Wren, must survive the monsoon in a leaking boat and cross the glacier route during the brief calving-season window. At the escarpment they find not treasure but the truth: records and remains that can finally name the dead. Orsen chooses justice over flight, delivering the evidence at the cost of his anonymity—and discovers that being seen was the thing he needed all along.
about_author: Sebastian Voss is the pen name of a former bush mechanic who spent six years flying supply runs across northern river country before turning to fiction. He writes adventure novels about people who live where maps run out.

chapters.title: Fuel and Rumors
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. He lands at a muddy strip town, delivering insulin and collecting gossip, establishing his rule: never stay two nights anywhere. A mining company man offers too much money for a charter he refuses. Emotional beat: restless competence masking dread.

chapters.title: The Dying Man's Bargain
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. In a trapping cabin he finds Elias Marsh, lungs full of blood, who trades a weathered map for one promise: carry it to his daughter Wren in Kestrel Landing. Orsen accepts against every instinct. Beat: reluctant compassion cracking his armor.

chapters.title: Two Nights Too Many
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Company men burn the strip town's fuel cache looking for Marsh's map; Orsen realizes his refusal made him a suspect. He flies out low through fog, hunted. Beat: paranoia sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Wren
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. In Kestrel Landing, Wren works a fish dock and wants nothing from her father—until a stranger lands with his map and his last words. She reads the margin notes and recognizes coordinates she's drawn since childhood. Beat: grief colliding with inheritance.

chapters.title: What the Map Shows
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The map marks the Lost Escarpment and something else: a surveyor's stamp from a camp that officially never existed. Wren reveals her father spent thirty years trying to prove a massacre there. Beat: the promise becomes a shared purpose.

chapters.title: The Stranger at the Dock
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. A charming drifter named Callum offers money, gear, and knowledge of the river rapids—he claims to have been to the escarpment once. Orsen doesn't trust him but needs him. Beat: uneasy alliance sealed by necessity.

chapters.title: Downriver
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. The plane is grounded by storm fronts; the only way in is the river. They buy a leaking freighter canoe and run the first rapids as the monsoon's first rain falls. Beat: exhilaration shadowed by pursuit.

chapters.title: Company Men
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Enforcers led by a quiet, methodical man named Harker catch up at a trading post. Callum talks their way past a checkpoint—but Wren sees him slip Harker a note. Beat: trust fracturing.

chapters.title: The Leaking Boat
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Monsoon peaks; the canoe takes on water faster than they can bail. They shelter in a flooded church, bailing in shifts while Orsen patches the hull with tarp and resin. Beat: endurance, and unexpected intimacy around a driftwood fire.

chapters.title: Callum's Story
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. He tells them he was a child laborer at the hidden camp—the massacre's youngest survivor—and that the company has hunted him since. Whether it's true or performance, even he seems unsure. Beat: sympathy extended cautiously.

chapters.title: Harker Closes
chapters.summary: Harker's POV. The enforcer tracks them upriver, revealing his own stake: he was ordered to erase the camp years ago and has been paying for it ever since. He wants the map destroyed before it names him. Beat: antagonist given weight.

chapters.title: Rapids of the Dead Camp
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. They shoot the gorge below the escarpment; the canoe tears open and they lose half their supplies, washing ashore beneath cliffs streaked with old survey paint. Beat: survival stripped to essentials.

chapters.title: Betrayal
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Callum steals the map and the last radio battery overnight, leaving a note claiming he'll trade it for safe passage out. Wren realizes she memorized the coordinates long ago. Beat: betrayal answered by quiet resourcefulness.

chapters.title: The Ascent
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Without the boat, they climb the goat track to the escarpment rim as the monsoon breaks and the calving season approaches—the glacier route opens in days, then closes. Beat: determination against exhaustion.

chapters.title: The Escarpment
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. On the plateau: collapsed barracks, a rusted survey vault, and rows of unmarked graves. Inside the vault are pay ledgers, orders signed by executives, and photographs naming the dead. Beat: grief transfigured into evidence.

chapters.title: Callum Returns
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Callum arrives with Harker behind him, having failed to make his own deal. Cornered, he confesses he sold the map's location to survive—and then turns on Harker when the enforcer raises his rifle. Beat: cowardice and courage in the same breath.

chapters.title: Standoff on the Ice
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. On the glacier tongue, Harker holds them at gunpoint as the ice begins to calve. Orsen gives him the choice he's been fleeing: be named in the record as an order-taker, or help carry the truth out. Beat: climax—justice offered outside the law.

chapters.title: Calving
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The glacier calves; the route opens for hours. Harker lowers his gun and guides them across collapsing ice as seracs fall like artillery. Callum is lost saving the evidence case. Beat: sacrifice amid spectacle.

chapters.title: The Crossing
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. They reach the far side with the vault contents intact, Harker walking beside them as a witness, not a captor. Orsen radios the outside world for the first time in years, using his real name. Beat: surrender of invisibility.

chapters.title: Deliverance
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. In the provincial capital, the evidence goes to a journalist and a judge; warrants issue against the company. Wren buries her father's map beside the names it vindicated. Beat: justice achieved, imperfectly.

chapters.title: Aftermath
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Testimony costs Orsen his license and his aliases; Harker faces his own reckoning. Wren asks what he'll do now that everyone knows his face. Beat: vulnerability without regret.

chapters.title: The Open Strip
chapters.summary: Orsen's POV. Months later, Orsen flies again—legally this time—with Wren navigating beside him, delivering medicine to the same strips. He no longer counts the nights he stays. Final beat: home is a direction, not a hiding place.
